metaTitle: UX Design Agency for Dubai & the UAE: Arabic RTL | Designit
metaDescription: UX and product design for Dubai and UAE companies: Arabic RTL done properly, luxury property experiences, regulated fintech flows and a shared working day.
h1: A UX design partner for the UAE, with the work to prove it
subtitle: We have delivered seven luxury property experiences in Dubai, including for Omniyat. That means Arabic RTL done properly, an understanding of how Gulf buyers evaluate, and a working time zone rather than a long lag.
author: Designit

cta.heading: Bilingual from the first wireframe
cta.body: Tell us about your audience and markets. We'll show you how we would structure the product for English and Arabic from the start.

sections.heading: What working in the UAE actually requires

items.title: Arabic is not a translation task
items.body: RTL mirrors layout, but numerals stay left-to-right, directional icons each need a decision and the visual centre of gravity shifts.

items.title: The audience is multilingual
items.body: One product may serve Emirati, South Asian, European and Chinese users. Designing for a single assumed reader excludes much of the market.

items.title: Regulated finance has its own perimeter
items.body: DIFC and ADGM run distinct regimes; flows built for another jurisdiction need real rework.

items.title: Premium is the baseline
items.body: In Dubai's property and luxury segments, adequate design reads as a downgrade.

sections.heading: How we work with UAE teams

items.title: Time zones
items.body: India is 1.5 hours ahead of Gulf Standard Time, so we share essentially the whole working day.

items.title: Bilingual design systems
items.body: One system with direction-aware tokens and components instead of two parallel design efforts.

items.title: Commercials
items.body: Quoted in USD or AED. Bilingual projects carry real additional scope, which we include upfront.

items.title: Local collaboration model
items.body: Remote, with live sessions in your working hours and RTL rules documented for your engineers.

sections.heading: Work in Dubai
sections.intro: Omniyat, LIV Residences, Orla Infinity, Opus, Anwa Aria, Ela and Vela Viento.

faq.q: Do you have actual UAE experience, or just a Dubai landing page?
faq.a: Actual experience: we designed seven luxury property experiences in Dubai through Rcentric, including work for Omniyat. We are an India-based studio serving UAE clients, not a Dubai-registered agency, and we would rather say that plainly.

faq.q: How do you handle Arabic RTL properly?
faq.a: By designing bidirectionally from the start. Layout flips, but numerals remain left-to-right, directional icons each need a decision, Arabic typography needs different vertical rhythm, and the entry point of every screen moves. We document these rules for engineering.

faq.q: Can you work with DIFC or ADGM-regulated entities?
faq.a: Yes. Both have their own onboarding, disclosure and record-keeping expectations, so we work directly with your compliance team from week one.

faq.q: What are your working hours relative to the UAE?
faq.a: India is 1.5 hours ahead of Gulf Standard Time, so we share essentially the entire working day.

faq.q: Do you work in Abu Dhabi and the wider Gulf?
faq.a: Yes. Our delivered work is concentrated in Dubai, but bilingual audiences, RTL, premium expectations and Gulf regulatory context carry across Abu Dhabi, Saudi Arabia and the wider GCC.

faq.q: Can you handle English and Arabic in one design system?
faq.a: That is what we recommend. A single bidirectional system costs less to build and maintain than two parallel efforts and prevents the language versions drifting apart.
